title: Influence of Doxycycline Use as Prophylaxis for Sexually Transmitted Infections on Bacterial Resistance and Gut Microbiota: MiDoxyR-PEP Study
official: Influence of Doxycycline Use as Prophylaxis for Sexually Transmitted Infections on Bacterial Resistance and Gut Microbiota: MiDoxyR-PEP Study
summary: Main objective: To study the impact of post-exposure prophylaxis with doxycycline (doxyPEP) among MSM and transgender women on the incidence of nasal colonization by Staphylococcus aureus with resistance mechanisms, the incidence of sexually transmitted infections (STIs), and to assess changes in gut microbiota following the initiation of doxyPEP in this population.
conditions: Colonization by methicillin-resistant S. aureus and gut microbiota in users of pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) and people living with HIV (PLHIV) with STIs.

interventions.name: Odefsey 200 mg/25 mg/25 mg film-coated tablets
Triumeq 50 mg/600 mg/300 mg film-coated tablets
Biktarvy 30 mg/120 mg/15 mg film-coated tablets

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Adult patients (18 years of age or older) who are MSM and transgender women, PrEP users, or people living with HIV.
2. Who have at least two of the following risk factors for contracting STIs, based on the recommendations of the Ministry of Health
3. More than 10 different sexual partners in the past year
4. Engaging in anal sex without a condom at least once in the past year
5. Drug use associated with having unprotected sex at least once in the past year.
6. Administration of post-exposure prophylaxis on more than one occasion in the past year.
7. Informed Consent Form
Exclusion criteria:
1. Patients under the age of 18.
2. Patients who are receiving long-term antimicrobial therapy, other than antiretroviral therapy or prophylaxis.
3. PrEP users who have been on treatment for less than 3 months, or people living with HIV who have a detectable viral load or have been on active antiretroviral therapy for less than 3 months.
4. Participation in another study involving the use of antimicrobials.
5. Patients with an allergy or intolerance to tetracyclines
